questions.question_text: Gravitational force between two masses:
questions.explanation: Gravitational force decreases as the separation between masses increases.

questions.question_text: The force that keeps a planet in orbit around the Sun is:
questions.explanation: Gravity provides the centripetal force needed for orbital motion.

questions.question_text: If the mass of the Sun is increased in the simulation, the gravitational pull on Earth:
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is directly proportional to the product of the masses.

questions.question_text: A satellite in a stable circular orbit must have velocity that is:
questions.explanation: Tangential velocity perpendicular to gravity produces stable orbital motion.

questions.question_text: Gravity acts between all objects that have mass.
questions.explanation: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation applies to all masses.

questions.question_text: Doubling the distance between two masses reduces the gravitational force to:
questions.explanation: Gravitational force follows an inverse-square law with distance.

questions.question_text: The Moon orbits Earth because:
options: There is no gravity in space
Earth's gravity provides the centripetal force
Air resistance keeps it in orbit
questions.correct_answer: Earth's gravity provides the centripetal force
questions.explanation: Earth's gravitational attraction continuously changes the Moon's direction of motion.

questions.question_text: If a planet moves too slowly for its distance from the Sun, it will fall toward the Sun.
questions.explanation: Insufficient orbital speed causes the object to spiral inward under gravity.

questions.question_text: Name the force that causes objects to attract each other due to their mass.
questions.explanation: Gravity is the attractive force between masses.

questions.question_text: What happens to orbital speed when a planet moves closer to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Planets move faster when closer to the Sun in their orbit.

questions.question_text: Gravitational potential energy of the skater depends on:
questions.explanation: Gravitational PE = mgh, so it depends on mass, gravity, and height.

questions.question_text: At the bottom of a frictionless track, most of the skater's energy is:
questions.explanation: At minimum height, PE is lowest and KE is greatest.

questions.question_text: Changing the reference height in the simulation changes:
options: The zero level for potential energy
questions.correct_answer: The zero level for potential energy
questions.explanation: Reference height defines where gravitational PE equals zero.

questions.question_text: When friction is enabled, total mechanical energy:
questions.explanation: Friction converts mechanical energy into thermal energy.

questions.question_text: Without friction, total mechanical energy is conserved as the skater moves along the track.
questions.explanation: Energy transforms between KE and PE but total mechanical energy stays constant.

questions.question_text: Doubling the skater's mass (at the same height) doubles the:
questions.explanation: PE = mgh, so doubling mass doubles potential energy.

questions.question_text: The energy bar graph shows that as height decreases:
questions.explanation: PE converts to KE as the skater moves to lower positions.

questions.question_text: A skater at rest at the top of a ramp has zero total energy.
questions.explanation: The skater has gravitational potential energy even when stationary.

questions.question_text: Write the formula for gravitational potential energy.
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy equals mass × gravity × height.

questions.question_text: What form of energy increases when friction is present?
questions.explanation: Friction converts mechanical energy into thermal (heat) energy.

question_bank.title: Circuit Construction Kit: DC — Physics Assessment

questions.question_text: In a series circuit, the current through each component is:
questions.explanation: In series, there is only one path so current is the same throughout.

questions.question_text: Adding more bulbs in series generally causes each bulb to:
questions.explanation: More resistance in series reduces total current and bulb brightness.

questions.question_text: The symbol for a resistor in a circuit diagram is:
questions.explanation: Resistors are represented by a zigzag symbol in circuit diagrams.

questions.question_text: If voltage is doubled and resistance stays constant, the current:
questions.explanation: From Ohm's Law (I = V/R), current is directly proportional to voltage.

questions.question_text: A switch can be used to open or close a circuit.
questions.explanation: Opening a switch breaks the circuit and stops current flow.

questions.question_text: In a parallel circuit, the voltage across each branch is:
options: The same as the supply voltage
questions.correct_answer: The same as the supply voltage
questions.explanation: In parallel, each branch is connected directly across the supply.

questions.question_text: A short circuit occurs when current takes a very low-resistance path.
questions.explanation: A short circuit bypasses components through a path of very low resistance.

questions.question_text: An ammeter is connected:
questions.explanation: Ammeters measure current and must be placed in series.

questions.question_text: State Ohm's Law as an equation.
questions.explanation: Voltage equals current multiplied by resistance.

questions.question_text: Name one component that provides electrical energy in a DC circuit.
questions.explanation: Batteries convert chemical energy to electrical energy in DC circuits.

question_bank.title: Wave on a String — Physics Assessment

questions.question_text: The maximum displacement of a wave from its rest position is called:
questions.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the equilibrium position.

questions.question_text: The distance between two consecutive crests is the:
questions.explanation: Wavelength (λ) is the distance between identical points on adjacent waves.

questions.question_text: Increasing the frequency of the wave source:
options: Decreases the number of waves per second
Increases the number of waves per second
Has no effect on the wave
questions.correct_answer: Increases the number of waves per second
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of complete waves passing a point per second.

questions.question_text: A wave on a string is an example of a:
questions.explanation: String particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave travel.

questions.question_text: Wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength.
questions.explanation: The wave equation is v = fλ.

questions.question_text: When a wave pulse reaches a fixed end, it:
questions.explanation: Reflection at a fixed end inverts the pulse.

questions.question_text: The period of a wave is the reciprocal of its frequency.
questions.explanation: Period T = 1/f.

questions.question_text: Doubling the amplitude of a wave:
questions.explanation: Wave energy is proportional to the square of amplitude.

questions.question_text: Write the wave equation relating speed, frequency, and wavelength.
questions.explanation: Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength.

questions.question_text: What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), or per second.

questions.question_text: The path of a projectile (ignoring air resistance) is:
questions.explanation: Projectile motion produces a parabolic trajectory.

questions.question_text: The horizontal component of velocity during flight (no air resistance):
questions.explanation: No horizontal force means horizontal velocity stays constant.

questions.question_text: At the highest point of the trajectory, the vertical velocity is:
questions.explanation: At maximum height, vertical velocity momentarily becomes zero.

questions.question_text: For maximum range on level ground (no air resistance), the ideal launch angle is:
questions.explanation: 45° gives maximum horizontal range for a given initial speed.

questions.question_text: Gravity only affects the vertical motion of a projectile.
questions.explanation: Gravity accelerates the projectile vertically; horizontal motion is unaffected.

questions.question_text: Increasing the initial launch speed (same angle) will:
options: Increase the range and maximum height
Make the projectile fall straight down
questions.correct_answer: Increase the range and maximum height
questions.explanation: Greater initial speed increases both horizontal and vertical components.

questions.question_text: Air resistance reduces the range of a projectile compared to the ideal case.
questions.explanation: Air resistance opposes motion and shortens the trajectory.

questions.question_text: The acceleration of a projectile in flight (ignoring air resistance) is:
questions.explanation: The only acceleration is gravitational acceleration downward.

questions.question_text: Name the two independent components used to analyse projectile motion.
questions.explanation: Projectile motion is analysed as separate horizontal and vertical motions.

questions.question_text: What force causes the projectile to accelerate downward?
questions.explanation: Gravity acts downward on the projectile throughout its flight.
